bug (plain English): A non-compliant NBD client can trigger an assertion (server crash) by sending BLOCK_STATUS without negotiated metacontexts.
fix (commit subject): nbd/server: Reject rather than assert on non-compliant BLOCK_STATUS
finding: title: Client-triggerable assertion failure when payload sent without meta contexts
finding: explanation: client->contexts.exp is only set by NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT, and nbd_check_meta_export only resets count (not exp) when the export changes. The receive path enters this function whenever the client sets NBD_CMD_FLAG_PAYLOAD_LEN in extended mode, regardless of whether NBD_FLAG_BLOCK_STAT_PAYLOAD was advertised. A client that negotiates extended headers but never sets meta contexts (contexts.exp == NULL), or sets them on export A and then does OPT_GO on export B, can send BLOCK_STATUS with the payload flag. The assert then aborts the server process (remote DoS).

bug (plain English): Emulating MOV r/m64, imm32 with a memory destination stores only the low 4 bytes of the sign-extended immediate.
fix (commit subject): hypervisor: x86: Store all 8 bytes for MOV r/m64, imm32
finding: title: MOV r/m64, imm32 now writes only 4 bytes to a memory destination
finding: explanation: mov_rm_imm now passes std::mem::size_of::<$bound>() as the operand size to set_op. Because Mov_rm64_imm32 is instantiated with u32, that size is 4. MOV r/m64, imm32 (REX.W C7 /0) must sign-extend the imm32 and store 8 bytes. When the destination is memory, which is the usual case since this emulator handles MMIO exits, set_op writes only the low 4 bytes. The upper 4 bytes are left unchanged and the sign extension is lost, so the device sees a 4-byte write instead of an 8-byte one. The old u32tou64 variant wrote the full sign-extended 64-bit value. Register destinations still work, assuming get_op returns the sign-extended immediate32to64 value and write_reg writes the full register.

bug (plain English): Prefault workers are released before their threads finish starting up, a race that makes large prefaults up to 4x slower.
fix (commit subject): vmm: prefault: Release workers only after their thread startup
finding: title: Concurrent thread total can still exceed machine_cores after scaling
finding: explanation: All regions are now prefaulted concurrently in one scope (previously sequentially, max 16 threads at a time). The cap rescales each region with cmp::max(1, threads * machine_cores / total), so every non-empty region keeps at least one thread. With more non-empty regions than cores (e.g. 6 regions on a 4-core / cgroup-limited host), more threads than cores run at once, all contending on mmap_lock and the hugetlb/page allocator locks. This defeats the stated budget.

bug (plain English): The memory-window range check includes the window's end, so an address one byte past the window is accepted and remapped (off-by-one).
fix (commit subject): raw/ntb: fix memory window bound in address remapping
finding: title: Partial multi-seg packet corrupts TX ring state and mbuf ownership
finding: explanation: The jump to `end_of_tx` can happen partway through a multi-segment packet: the ring fills, a descriptor has len 0, or ioremap fails. By then earlier segments have advanced `txq->last_used`, been added to `tx_used`, and been stored in `sw_ring`, but `nb_tx` and `nb_tx_free` were not updated. If `nb_tx > 0`, `used_cnt` is published with trailing segments that have no EOP flag. The peer then joins them with the next packet. If `nb_tx == 0`, those slots are skipped without being published, so the next call writes used entries and `used_cnt` past descriptors the peer never sees filled. In both cases the caller still owns the unsent mbuf (it was not counted), while `sw_ring` points to it. `ntb_enqueue_cleanup` later frees it, which is a double free or use-after-free.
